content:
# OPC 一人企业方法论

A 9-skill operating system for turning personal expertise, assets, and channels into a lightweight one-person business loop.

## Method Overview

| Stage | Goal |
| --- | --- |
| Resource Audit | 盘点可复用资源与能力 |
| Niche Positioning | 找到更清晰的定位切口 |
| Value Proposition | 把能力翻译成可购买价值 |
| Business Model | 设计轻资产交付方式 |
| Funnel Design | 建立获客到转化路径 |
| Productization | 将服务产品化 |
| Pricing | 形成价格与套餐结构 |
| Content Engine | 用内容驱动信任与线索 |
| Iteration | 根据反馈优化闭环 |

## Workflow

1. Start with resource audit instead of jumping directly to product ideas.
2. Narrow positioning before designing offers.
3. Build the funnel and product package together.
4. Use content and iteration skills to keep the business loop improving.

## Best For

- Solo builders, consultants, educators, and creators.
- People with existing expertise but unclear packaging.
- Lightweight business design before hiring, fundraising, or building heavy software.

# GPT Image 2

A focused image generation and editing skill for GPT Image 2 workflows. It supports direct Garden execution, host-native image tools, or prompt-only advisory mode.

## Runtime Modes

| Mode | Use When |
| --- | --- |
| Garden Local | The environment can call an OpenAI-compatible image API directly |
| Host-Native | The host app provides its own image generation or editing tool |
| Advisor | No image tool is available, so the skill produces a reusable prompt |

## Best For

- Posters, UI concepts, product visuals, information graphics, technical diagrams, avatars, comics, storyboards, and image editing prompts.
- Turning vague visual goals into structured prompts.
- Choosing the right template before asking an image model to render.

## Workflow

1. Detect the runtime mode.
2. Decide whether the task is generation, editing, or prompt advisory.
3. Pick the closest visual template.
4. Render a complete prompt with format, subject, style, constraints, and output notes.
5. Save or hand off the result according to the active mode.

## Output Shape

Prompt files, generated images when tools are available, or advisor-ready prompt packages when generation cannot run locally.

# Kami — Professional Document Typesetting

Typeset professional documents such as resumes, one-pagers, white papers, letters, portfolios, and slide decks.

## Best For

- Turning plain text into polished PDFs, HTML pages, or PPTX-style decks.
- Documents that need a warm editorial tone and strong typography.
- Workflows that require rendering and visual verification before delivery.

## Document Templates

| Template | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Resume | Career profile and applications |
| One-pager | Compact product or service summary |
| White paper | Long-form technical or business document |
| Letter | Formal correspondence |
| Portfolio | Project and case presentation |
| Slide deck | Presentation-ready narrative |

## Design Direction

Warm parchment surfaces, ink-blue accents, serif-led hierarchy, and careful spacing. Chinese, English, and Japanese typography use best-effort font choices when available.

## Workflow

1. Choose the document target and audience.
2. Structure the content into sections and hierarchy.
3. Render the output artifact.
4. Visually verify pages for placeholders, overflow, orphan lines, and layout issues.

# Impeccable Design Quality

A design-quality system that teaches AI agents to avoid common interface mistakes before they generate or review UI.

## Core Idea

Most AI-generated interfaces fail in predictable ways: weak hierarchy, decorative gradients, poor spacing, nested cards, tiny type, low contrast, and generic copy. Impeccable names these patterns and turns them into repeatable checks.

## Quality Dimensions

| Dimension | Focus |
| --- | --- |
| Visual Expression | Scale, rhythm, hierarchy |
| Design Systems | Tokens, accessibility, consistency |
| Spatial Layout | Composition, spacing, alignment |
| Responsive Design | Fluid layouts and touch targets |
| Interaction Design | States, feedback, affordance |
| Motion & Polish | Transitions and micro-interactions |
| Content Quality | Clarity, voice, error text |

## Command Families

- Creation: /create, /shape, /craft.
- Evaluation: /evaluate, /audit, /critique.
- Refinement: /refine, /polish, /bolder, /simplify, /distill.
- Production: /harden, /system.
- Context: /teach, /extract, /impeccable.

## Best For

Use it before or after UI generation when the page needs stronger taste, clearer hierarchy, and fewer generic AI design patterns.

# UI UX Pro Max

AI design intelligence for building professional UI/UX across multiple platforms, product types, and implementation stacks.

## Best For

- New product pages, landing pages, dashboards, and mobile/web app screens.
- Choosing a design system direction before implementation begins.
- Reviewing existing UI for UX, accessibility, interaction, navigation, forms, and data visualization issues.
- Matching product category, audience, style, color, typography, and stack constraints.

## Core Capabilities

| Capability | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Design system generation | Produce pattern, style, color, typography, effects, and anti-pattern guidance |
| Industry reasoning rules | Match recommendations to SaaS, finance, healthcare, e-commerce, services, creative, and emerging tech products |
| UX checklist library | Review forms, navigation, feedback, accessibility, charts, and responsive behavior |
| Stack-aware guidance | Adapt recommendations for React, Next.js, Vue, SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter, and related stacks |

## Workflow

1. Analyze the product type, audience, platform, and requested interface.
2. Generate or retrieve a design system before writing UI.
3. Supplement with domain searches for style, color, typography, charts, UX rules, or stack-specific details.
4. Implement with the chosen design vocabulary and avoid category-specific anti-patterns.
5. Review the result against contrast, focus, motion, navigation, layout, and responsive checks.

## Output Shape

A structured UI direction, implementation checklist, and review rubric that can guide a build or critique a finished screen.

## Boundaries

This skill is a design intelligence layer. It does not replace visual QA in the browser, and it should be paired with actual screenshots or rendered pages when judging final polish.

# Web Design Engineer

Build high-quality visual web artifacts using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React: pages, dashboards, prototypes, slide decks, UI mockups, data visualizations, and animated demos.

## Best For

- Visual front-end deliverables where taste, layout, motion, and responsive behavior matter.
- Turning product ideas, screenshots, PRDs, or existing code into usable web artifacts.
- Creating polished prototypes that can be inspected in a browser.

## Workflow

1. Understand the product context, audience, output type, constraints, and fidelity target.
2. Gather design context from screenshots, code, references, or an existing design system.
3. Declare the color, type, spacing, radius, shadow, and motion direction before building.
4. Produce an early visible draft when direction is uncertain.
5. Implement complete components, states, accessibility, and responsive behavior.
6. Verify text fit, focus states, interactions, and layout across viewports.

## Technical Notes

- Prefer CSS Grid, Flexbox, custom properties, and responsive constraints.
- Use real visual assets where the domain calls for inspection or specificity.
- Keep controls complete and keyboard-accessible.
- Avoid generic AI visual clichés, meaningless fake metrics, and decorative clutter.

content:
# Editorial Card Screenshot

Turn dense source text into a screenshot-ready editorial information card with strong hierarchy, compact spacing, and a magazine-like reading path.

## Best For

- High-density summary cards for articles, rankings, analysis, or social sharing.
- Fixed-ratio compositions such as 3:4, 4:3, 1:1, 16:9, and 9:16.
- Cases where text clarity matters more than decorative illustration.

## Workflow

1. Judge whether the source content is sparse, medium-density, or dense.
2. Choose a layout skeleton that matches the target ratio.
3. Group content into primary insight, supporting modules, and footer/meta details.
4. Write screenshot-ready HTML with fixed canvas dimensions.
5. Check for overlaps, dead space, unreadable type, and monotonous equal-weight blocks.

## Output Shape

- One density judgment sentence.
- Complete HTML with embedded CSS.
- Optional screenshot command when an image export is requested.

## Boundaries

This skill is optimized for static editorial cards. It should not be used for long scrolling pages, interactive dashboards, or generic landing pages.

content:
# Blueprinter

Generate technical diagrams with a flat engineering blueprint style: precise borders, aligned grids, restrained typography, and high data density.

## Best For

- Architecture diagrams, system flows, infrastructure maps, and technical specification sheets.
- Cases where the diagram should feel objective and inspectable rather than decorative.
- HTML/CSS diagrams that need to be easy to edit after generation.

## Visual Rules

- Use white or very light canvases with thin slate borders.
- Keep components rectangular, aligned, and labelled with clear hierarchy.
- Use monospace for paths, IDs, protocol names, and implementation details.
- Prefer straight or orthogonal connector lines.
- Avoid shadows, blur, gradients, decorative backgrounds, and marketing-style composition.

## Workflow

1. Identify the system components and their relationships.
2. Group components into layers or zones.
3. Choose a grid before drawing individual nodes.
4. Add labels, badges, and connectors only where they clarify the system.
5. Verify alignment, spacing, and text fit at the target viewport.

## Output Shape

A standalone HTML/CSS diagram or diagram section with reusable CSS variables, component boxes, connector lines, and compact technical labels.

# App Icon Minimalist

Create clear app icons with a practical three-step method for non-designers. The goal is to reach a shippable icon quickly, then refine only when the product needs it.

## Best For

- MVP or side-project icons where clarity matters more than ornament.
- iOS, Android, web, or PWA launch assets.
- Users who have an app concept but no design tool workflow.

## Workflow

1. Reduce the app to one core function.
2. Translate that function into one simple symbol.
3. Place it in a platform-safe frame and test at small sizes.

## Output Shape

- Core function summary.
- Suggested symbol and visual metaphor.
- Color and layout guidance.
- Export-size reminders for the target platform.

## Boundaries

This skill is for icon direction and iteration guidance. It does not replace a full brand identity system or produce final raster exports by itself.
